what: highlight "In 2020, the value of government debt worldwide was US$87.4 trillion"
said: By twenty twenty, governments around the world owed about eighty-seven trillion dollars. That was ninety-nine percent of everything the whole planet produced in a year.

what: highlight "In 2018, global government debt reached the equivalent of $66 trillion"
said: Only two years earlier, it had been sixty-six trillion. The pile grows faster than almost anything else on Earth.

what: highlight "Global Debt Reaches a Record $226 Trillion"
said: And that is only governments. Add the debts of companies and households, and one famous headline put total global debt at a record two hundred twenty-six trillion dollars.

what: highlight "Government debt may be owed to domestic residents, as well as to foreign residents."
said: Government debt works exactly the same way. Every bond a government sells is a promise held by someone else. That someone can be at home or abroad.

what: highlight "Actors that issue sovereign credit include private investors, commercial banks"
said: So who holds these promises? Private investors, banks, big development banks like the World Bank, and other governments.

what: highlight "234.9% of the country's gross domestic product"
said: Japan has the biggest debt of any rich nation, compared to the size of its economy. In March twenty twenty-five, it was almost two hundred thirty-five percent of GDP.

what: highlight "1,324 trillion yen"
said: In yen, the number is so big it is hard to say. One thousand three hundred twenty-four trillion yen.

what: highlight "88.1 per cent was held domestically"
said: Because Japan mostly owes the money to itself. At the end of twenty twenty-four, eighty-eight percent of its government debt was held inside Japan.

what: highlight "The largest holders were the Bank of Japan (46.3 per cent)"
said: The biggest holder of all was Japan's own central bank, the Bank of Japan. It held about forty-six percent.

what: highlight "domestic insurance companies (15.6 per cent), and domestic banks (14.5 per cent)"
said: After that came Japanese insurance companies and Japanese banks. In other words, the savings of Japanese families.

what: highlight "largely insulates the prices and yields of such bonds from the effects of the global bond market"
said: Because so much of the debt is held at home, Japanese bond prices are protected from swings in the global market.

what: highlight "The Public Finance Act prohibits the Bank of Japan from buying government bonds"
said: Japan's own history also shows the danger of this setup. Its law now bans the central bank from buying bonds directly from the government.

what: highlight "brought about violent inflation by their public bond purchases"
said: That rule exists because, around World War Two, central bank bond buying helped cause violent inflation in Japan.

what: highlight "Ben Bernanke used the phrase"
said: In twenty oh five, the head of the Federal Reserve, Ben Bernanke, gave this a name. He called it a global saving glut. A glut means too much of something.

what: highlight "significant increase in the global supply of saving"
said: He worried about a big increase in savings around the world, flowing into America and pushing interest rates down.

what: highlight "pension funding to make provision for an impending increase in the number of retirees"
said: One reason for all that saving surprised people. Many countries were getting older, so they were saving for a coming wave of retirees. Pension funds like Carol's, all over the world.

what: highlight "as the supply of savings outstrips its demand"
said: When that much saving looks for a home, it pushes interest rates down. Too much money chasing too few safe places to put it.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "foreigners held 33% ($7 trillion out of $21.6 trillion)"
said: So how much of America's debt is owed abroad? In December twenty twenty, foreigners held about one third of the publicly held debt.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "the top three December 2020 national holders of American public debt were Japan"
said: The top three that year were Japan, with one point two trillion dollars, China, with one point one trillion, and the United Kingdom.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "$4.1 trillion (59.2%) belonged to foreign governments"
said: More than half of that foreign money belonged to foreign governments. The rest belonged to foreign investors, like banks and funds.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "rising from 13% of the public debt in 1988 to 34% in 2015"
said: The foreign government share had grown a lot. It went from thirteen percent of the public debt in nineteen eighty-eight to thirty-four percent in twenty fifteen.

source: Wikipedia, National debt of the United States
what: highlight "foreign ownership has retreated both in percent of total debt and total dollar amounts"
said: But in more recent years, foreign ownership has been shrinking, both as a share and in total dollars.

what: highlight "Around 70% of Japanese government bonds are purchased by the Bank of Japan"
said: In Japan, around seventy percent of new government bonds have been bought by the Bank of Japan.

what: highlight "in the 1920s Weimar Germany suffered from hyperinflation"
said: In the nineteen twenties, Germany printed money to pay off debts after World War One. The result was hyperinflation, where prices doubled again and again.

what: highlight "a bond with no maturity"
said: Some governments have even sold bonds with no end date at all. They just pay interest forever. A country can carry debt for as long as lenders keep trusting it.

what: highlight "debt-to-GDP ratios above 77% for developed countries"
said: Economists at the World Bank studied one hundred countries. They found that when debt went above about seventy-seven percent of GDP in rich countries, future growth tended to slow down.

what: highlight "Countries have at times escaped some of the real burden of their debt through inflation ."
said: The quiet way is inflation. Governments have often escaped part of their debt by letting prices rise, so each old dollar they owe is worth less.

what: highlight "Philip II of Spain defaulted on debt four times"
said: It has happened many times in history. King Philip the Second of Spain, ruler of one of the richest empires on Earth, defaulted four times.

what: highlight "several Latin American countries that had recently entered the bond market in London defaulted"
said: In the eighteen twenties, several new Latin American countries borrowed in London and then defaulted too.

what: highlight "state to default was Arkansas, which defaulted in 1933"
said: Even an American state has done it. The last state to default was Arkansas, in nineteen thirty-three, during the Great Depression.

what: highlight "which reached 127% of GDP in 2009"
said: By two thousand nine, its debt had reached one hundred twenty-seven percent of its economy. Lenders got scared, and interest rates on Greek debt shot up.

what: highlight "on debt owed to private banks in 2011"
said: Greece needed rescue loans in two thousand ten, two thousand twelve and two thousand fifteen. Private lenders were forced to accept a fifty percent cut on what they were owed.

what: highlight "Unemployment reached nearly 25%"
said: Regular Greeks paid a huge price. Wages fell nearly twenty percent, and unemployment reached nearly twenty-five percent.

what: highlight "The government enacted 12 rounds of tax increases, spending cuts, and reforms from 2010-16"
said: The government passed twelve rounds of tax increases and spending cuts. There were riots and nationwide protests.

what: highlight "the Greek debt-to-GDP ratio rose up from 127% to 179%"
said: And here is the cruel part. Because the economy shrank so much, the debt compared to the economy actually rose, from one hundred twenty-seven to one hundred seventy-nine percent.

what: highlight "Greece became the first developed country to fail to make an IMF loan repayment"
said: On June thirtieth, twenty fifteen, Greece became the first developed country ever to miss a loan payment to the International Monetary Fund.

what: highlight "In June 2026, Greece repaid a further €6.9bn"
said: Greece recovered slowly. In June twenty twenty-six, it even paid back part of its first rescue loan early.
